message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have $1137 and five properties. No monopolies are active. Other players hold significant cash and railroads.

Virginia, Tennessee, and New York are bank-owned. I need them to complete the pink and orange monopolies. I will keep cash and avoid trading Vermont to p4.

I am evaluating trade offers. p4 has cash but few properties. Completing the light blue set would drain money I need for the pink and orange monopolies. I am also considering a deal with p2.

p2's yellow properties are not useful for completing my sets. p3's Boardwalk is too expensive without Park Place. No trade looks profitable. I am now considering offering cash to p4 for specific properties.

I am now considering a specific trade with p4. I would offer cash for both Oriental and Connecticut. That would cost roughly $300 to $400, leaving me with about $700 to $800. I could then buy Virginia for $160 and build on it.

I rejected the trade with p4. They would use a light blue monopoly to build on it, and I cannot afford to help them. Water Works for Boardwalk is also unprofitable. I will end my turn.

I am now calculating the rent and house costs for a light blue monopoly. The set totals $320 in purchase price and $50 per house. I need to determine if buying it from p4 is worth the investment.

The light blue set would cost roughly $700 to $800 to acquire. That is too expensive when orange and pink monopolies offer far better returns. p4 will not sell it either, since they want to hold color properties for future monopoly trades.
